title: 256 10-round BDK+10: aes256-10r-subkey-cc-partial-bdk2010

target.description: 10-round AES-256 variant starting at an odd-numbered round, with source omitted-final-MixColumns convention. The endpoint recovers only the source-stated subkey/key information; no unreported 256-bit completion is appended. Output: 35 bits of information from five subkey bytes. The source explicitly starts at round 1 and ends at round 10; its displayed figure renumbers local rounds.

setting.key_relation: For the exact rounds 1–10 variant choose Delta(K^2)=(b,b,b,b) and Delta(K^3)=(a,0,a,0), with a=(alpha,0,0,0)^T, b=MC((beta,0,0,0)^T), Pr[alpha -> beta]=2^-6. All round subkeys remain AES-256-schedule-consistent; this nonlinear induced master-key relation is stronger than fixed-XOR related master keys.
setting.plaintext_model: Source CC accounting at 2^44; plaintext identities, paired related-key queries and total oracle calls are distinguished in the resource note.
assumptions: The related-subkey relation, where used, is stronger than a fixed XOR master-key relation but all expanded subkeys remain consistent with their master key.

time.note: Source headline/table work; Section 4.1.3 explicitly compares oracle encryptions with simple lookups. Units for other endpoints are not independently normalized.

data.note: Table 1/endpoint native data convention, not silently treated as aggregate oracle queries. Section 5.2 queries 2^44 ciphertexts under each key, so the total number of decryption calls is 2^45.

memory.note: Table 1 numeric memory; the table does not specify a uniform byte/word unit. Nine-round full recovery separately distinguishes small RAM from external data storage.

preprocessing.note: The source does not separately quantify this resource for this configuration.

success.description: No numerical success is stated for the35-bit partial-subkey endpoint at data2^44. Four right pairs are expected; the source does not specify their joint acquisition/output distribution. The2^-32 wrong-vote statement remains local. Five two-candidate bytes yield the source35-bit information output, not complete master-key recovery. The57% in Section4.1.3 and0.63 in Section6.1 belong to different attacks and budgets.

components.description: Section5.2: source32-bit terminal-state filter, reducing2^76 cross-pairs to2^44. The cross-pair count is not the query count.
Section5.2: source product for seven specified S-box transitions,2^(-7*6); the resulting four right pairs are an expectation, not a distribution of recovery outcomes.
Section5.2: fixed64-bit plaintext-difference test for wrong pairs, leaving source expected2^12 candidates.

Section5.2 explicitly assigns2^-32 to four wrong pairs suggesting the same values in its candidate-vote model. This is a local false-consensus claim, not a bound for all key-difference guesses or a35-bit recovery success probability.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit. Local pair filters, conditional trails, weak-pair incidence and expected counts keep their own experiment; correlation is not a decision probability. Existing conflicts, resources, targets, settings and full-audit gates remain unchanged.
